findings.title: #979 inverts the read contract and leaves the existing regression cell that pins the old one RED on the branch
findings.evidence: Ticket AC: "Existing callers that only test for an active authority are unaffected by the added fields." The branch leaves packages/db/tests/depreciation-history.test.mjs:456 (cell p651.authority.retire_unsigned) failing at line 487: assert.equal(env.authority, null, "...and the READ is honest: a retired-only client shares the 'none proposed' state with a fresh one, which is what the surface already renders"). Re-run on the lane rig (clara_l04, 127.0.0.1:55744, chain 0001..0234 + 0247..0251), full 55-import gate chain: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 $GATES tests/depreciation-history.test.mjs` -> `not ok 11 - p651.authority.retire_unsigned`, actual = {id, status:'retired', retired_reason:'p651 wrong cadence, withdrawn before signature', retired_by, retired_at, authority_from:'2026-09-01', ...}, expected null. Reproduced again in a whole-packages/db run (`not ok 776`), and again in the eight-file FA batch (76 tests, 75 pass, 1 fail - this one). The cause is 0251's fallback select (packages/db/migrations/0251_fa_authority_retired_read.sql:173-177), which is exactly what the ticket asked for; what is missing is the corresponding update to the cell that encodes the superseded contract. wave2-lane04-ticket979.md's gate table does not list depreciation-history.test.mjs at all - the one file whose contract the ticket inverts was never re-run.
findings.required_fix: In #979's own commits, recut p651.authority.retire_unsigned (depreciation-history.test.mjs:456-490, including the comment quoting the F6 note) to the new three-state contract: a retired-only client returns THAT authority, and the 'lane reopens' fact is proved by propose/sign succeeding rather than by authority === null. Then re-run tests/depreciation-history.test.mjs with the full gate chain and record the count.

findings.title: #972's watermark predicate puts a session clock into the birth trigger, breaking two pinned clock-roster censuses that the branch leaves RED
findings.evidence: Ticket Desired behavior: "The belt never births a register row from an entry posted before the enrolling account's watermark, on any firing, including a re-fire caused by an UPDATE such as the reversed_by stamp. Reversal is otherwise unchanged." Nothing in the ticket asks for a clock read. 0247_fa_birth_watermark.sql:78/262 splices `coalesce(new.approved_at, now()) >= fp.enrolled_at` into clara._tf_fa_acquisition_birth. Re-run on the lane rig, full gate chain: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 $GATES tests/x42b2-r7-s5-clock.test.mjs tests/x42b2-s5c-clock.test.mjs` -> 4 tests, 2 pass, 2 fail: `not ok - x42.r7.s5c.5` (x42b2-r7-s5-clock.test.mjs:211) and `not ok - x42.s5c.6` (x42b2-s5c-clock.test.mjs:369). Set-diff of each cell's actual vs expected arm-(D) bare-token roster, computed from the run output, is exactly ["_tf_fa_acquisition_birth"] in both, with nothing missing. All three x42 files (x42b2-r7-s5-clock.test.mjs, x42b2-s5c-clock.test.mjs, x42-s5-helpers.mjs) are byte-identical to BASE (`git diff 23cfad94...HEAD -- <files>` empty), so the reds are the migration's, not a test edit's. packages/db/tests/x42-s5-helpers.mjs:1161-1166 still states in prose that the birth trigger carries no clock. #972's own report (wave2-lane04-ticket972.md) lists neither x42 file in its gates; the reds were discovered later by #977's implementer and recorded as "follow-up 0" rather than fixed.
findings.required_fix: Inside #972's own scope, either (a) keep the birth body clock-free - the ticket's rule is about the entry's own post date, and clara.journal_entries.approved_at is nullable with no constraint tying it to status='approved' (measured: 0 approved rows with a null approved_at on clara_l04), so a non-clock fallback such as new.posting_date is available - or (b) extend arm (D)'s pinned roster and correct the FA_ACQUISITION_0216_CLOCK_NAMES prose in packages/db/tests/x42-s5-helpers.mjs, in the same ticket, and re-run both x42 cells.

findings.title: #976's fold moves both completion refusals behind _reserve_op and the client/asset walls, reversing a property 0227 documented as deliberate - and deletes the sentence that documented it
findings.evidence: Ticket Desired behavior: "Every caller keeps its current signature, grants and refusal codes; only the duplication is removed." 0227_depreciation_history.sql:649-657 and :684-692 - the two spliced copies the fold replaces - each carry the comment "Refused BEFORE the op key is reserved, so a retry is clean." On the branch, both doors now reserve first: measured off pg_proc on clara_l04, clara._fa_complete_particulars_core has _reserve_op at offset 293 and clara._fa_assert_particulars_completable at offset 1138, with the client lookup, the advisory lock and the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in between; clara.complete_fixed_asset_particulars is the same shape (see its live prosrc). The new shared routine clara._fa_assert_particulars_completable carries 0227's comment for the change-class arm verbatim EXCEPT that the "Refused BEFORE the op key is reserved, so a retry is clean." sentence is gone. Two observable consequences the ticket did not ask for and no cell covers: (1) a call carrying a revision-only key plus an unknown client or asset now refuses CLR11 client_not_found / asset_not_found instead of CLR37 fa_change_class_on_completion; (2) the refusal now happens after an op_receipts insert - clara._reserve_op is a plain `insert ... on conflict do nothing`, so it rolls back with the RAISE in the normal one-statement call, but nothing on the branch proves that, and the estate's own written statement of the property was removed rather than re-derived. wave2-lane04-ticket976.md argues (2) from 0004_governed_fns.sql's header; the argument is plausible but untested.
findings.required_fix: Either keep the change-class arm before _reserve_op (the one routine can expose a pre-reservation arm and a post-lock arm, both owned in one place, which still satisfies AC1/AC2 'only one place contains the check'), or add a cell that drives a change-class refusal through each door and then proves clara.op_receipts holds no row for that op_key, and restore 0227's sentence to the shared routine with its new justification.

findings.title: #972 AC5's green was taken on a throwaway clone that no longer exists; x41.s4 is still RED on the lane rig
findings.evidence: Ticket AC: "On a freshly built family, x41.s4 reports zero unexplained differences at all three as-ofs, allow-list unchanged at one entry." Re-run on the lane rig, full gate chain, in a 13-file batch (143 tests, 141 pass, 1 fail, 1 skip): `not ok 128 - x41.s4 the x41-family-scoped fa_register_tie sweep at three as-ofs`. wave2-lane04-ticket972.md states the AC5 green was measured on a template copy (clara_l04_s4) in which four pre-0247 register rows were deleted with clara._tf_fixed_assets_immutable_0017 temporarily disabled, and that the clone was then dropped - so the figure cannot be re-taken. The other half of the AC IS verifiable and holds: packages/db/tests/x41-round35-tie.test.mjs is byte-identical to BASE (`git diff 23cfad94...HEAD -- <file>` empty), so ALLOWED_RED is unchanged at one entry.
findings.required_fix: The integrator re-takes AC5 on the disposable from-scratch cluster (0001 -> 0251) and records the sweep's own summary line, so the ticket's last acceptance criterion rests on a reproducible measurement rather than on a dropped clone.

findings.title: #979 pins, without closing, a read/mock divergence on authority_from that the same testid depends on
findings.evidence: 0251 merges authority_from onto the returned object ONLY on the retired arm (packages/db/migrations/0251_fa_authority_retired_read.sql:195-197), and p979.preferred asserts by key absence that a live authority carries none of it. apps/web/components/registers/fa-authority-ceremony.tsx renders the window on `(au.status === "live" || au.status === "retired") && au.authority_from`, and apps/web/e2e/depreciation-mock.mjs:228 returns authority_from on a LIVE authority, which apps/web/e2e/depreciation-walk.spec.ts:67 then asserts through `fa-authority-window`. So the live half of that testid is exercised only against a payload the real read does not produce. This predates #979 (it is #651's), and #979's own comment in apps/web/lib/registers/depreciation.ts names it as "a different ticket's widening" - flagged here because #979 reuses that exact testid for the retired case.
findings.required_fix: No change required of #979. Worth a follow-up ticket: either surface authority_from on the live arm too, or correct the e2e mock so the walk stops asserting a field the door never returns.

summary: Five tickets, all implemented against the newest brief (the 2026-09-20 owner rulings on #977 and #979 were correctly taken as the contract). #973 and #977 are clean on this axis. Three findings need a fix before integration: #979 inverted clara.get_depreciation_authority's contract without recutting the regression cell that pins the old one, so p651.authority.retire_unsigned is red on the branch (blocker); #972's watermark predicate introduced a session-clock read into the birth trigger and left two pinned clock-roster censuses red (major); #976's fold moved both completion refusals behind _reserve_op and the client/asset walls, reversing a property 0227 documented as deliberate and deleting the sentence that said so (major). Two minors and two notes besides.
